html:
Albert Einstein was a German born physicist whose theories of relativity changed how science understands space, time, gravity and energy. He won the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for explaining the photoelectric effect, a founding step in quantum theory.

He was born in Ulm and grew up in Munich. He studied in Zurich, and when no university would hire him he took a job checking patents in Bern. There, in 1905, his "miracle year", he published four papers:

  • Light comes in packets, quanta, which explained the photoelectric effect.
  • Brownian motion, the jiggling of small particles in water, as proof that atoms exist.
  • Special relativity: the speed of light is the same for every observer, so time and length depend on how fast you move.
  • Mass and energy are equivalent, the formula E = mc².

His general theory of relativity (1915) described gravity as the curving of space and time by mass. When observations of a solar eclipse in 1919 confirmed that starlight bends near the Sun, he became world famous. Satellite navigation systems today must correct for both theories.

He replaced the mechanics of Isaac Newton for very high speeds and strong gravity, but he never accepted the randomness of the quantum theory he had helped start. As he put it in a letter, God does not throw dice.

He was Jewish and a pacifist, and the Nazis attacked his "Jewish physics". When Hitler took power in 1933 he left Germany for Princeton in the United States. In 1939 he signed a letter warning President Roosevelt that Germany might build an atomic bomb, which helped lead to the Manhattan Project, though he did not work on it. He later regretted the letter and campaigned against nuclear weapons until his death in 1955.
